## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Impact window:** 2026-03-14 02:14:18Z – 03:59:27Z (ongoing at end of log, ~1h45m+), 530 failed requests (`ERROR access ... 503`), affecting `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/checkout` across all upstream services (billing/orders/catalog/accounts-svc). Gateway only — worker fleet (`worker.log`, 4 replicas) unaffected, all jobs completed ok throughout.

**Root cause:** Connection pool exhaustion. Gateway's pool is fixed at `size=20`. Every 503 is paired with `ERROR pool ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)` — the wait queue grew from 13 at onset to 74+ by 03:59, response times climbing 660ms → 850ms.

**Trigger:** `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak) — *"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"*, deployed 02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z. Config generation 118→119 applied at 02:13:41Z, flipping `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` (also bumped `upstreamMs: 2000->2500`). First `WARN pool acquire slow` at 02:14:14Z, first 503 at 02:14:18Z — 4 seconds later. The per-request isolation change is preventing pooled connections from being released/reused, exhausting the pool within seconds.

**Rollback:** Revert **dep-4471** (gateway config change) — restore `gateway.pool.perRequest: true -> false`.

Not implicated: dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41Z) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc, 03:20Z) both land after onset and don't touch gateway/pool config.
